value.rationale: PASS: Distinguishing physically distinct fluctuating transport environments from observed particle tracks is an explicit mathematical inference problem. Exact matching of all covariance and fourth-order multi-time information demonstrates a complete low-order information barrier, the unique sixth crossing provides a sharp exception to an otherwise usable sixth-order discriminator, and the strictly positive eighth gap identifies a universally working next-order observable at the blind spot. The full classification applies to all positive time, not an arbitrarily selected finite parameter point; no paper-sized downstream theorem is required.
